fields.impact:
I am the creator and primary maintainer of Quenderin, an MIT-licensed app for running open language models on users' own devices. It is available on iPhone and Mac, with Android source and downloadable Windows/Linux previews. It combines model selection, integrity-checked installation and cross-platform parity checks in a public codebase that other developers can inspect and adapt.

I am requesting discretionary Ecosystem Impact Track consideration. Adoption is early: App Store Connect reports 69 first-time downloads for July 22-October 19, 2026, including 37 for September 20-October 19. These are app acquisitions, not active-user counts or package-registry downloads. I am not claiming large downstream dependency counts.

I maintain native model and engine integrations, verified multipart downloads, memory admission checks, privacy disclosures, tests and release provenance. Recent public work includes:
https://github.com/alikatgh/quenderin/pull/163
https://github.com/alikatgh/quenderin/pull/164
https://github.com/alikatgh/quenderin/pull/167

The gap it addresses is practical access to open models on personal hardware, including the installation, compatibility and correctness work needed across different platforms. I would welcome consideration based on this useful, auditable implementation and its ongoing maintenance.
fields.use:
I would use Claude Code and Claude Max for maintaining the public repository: reviewing model-loader and parser changes, reasoning through memory and cancellation boundaries, creating regression tests for partial or corrupt model downloads, checking Swift/Kotlin/TypeScript behavior against shared test vectors, triaging reproducible issues and reviewing dependency updates.

I would also improve contributor setup and architecture documentation so others can build and understand the project. I would reproduce findings, inspect proposed diffs, run targeted tests and check affected user journeys before merging or releasing. My priority is sustained correctness and cross-platform support as new open-model architectures arrive. I would keep work within the subscription's included usage.
fields.other: I also authored six published Flask utilities: flask-supercache, flask-i18n-pro, flask-querymonitor, flask-ratelimit-simple, flask-security-headers and flask-imagekit. PyPIStats records 400 combined downloads excluding mirrors for Sep 21-Oct 20, 2026; these are not unique-user counts. Their PyPI pages link to public wallmarkets repositories. Related Go work: https://github.com/alikatgh/safeheaders-go

notes: GitHub verified identity and repository in the live form; this is not acceptance or threshold qualification.
App Store acquisition evidence is not package-registry downloads or active-user counts.
No API usage, paid plan, subscription activation or overages have been enabled.
